t: AI prompts for writing emails
n: Turn rough notes into an email
x:
Write an email from my notes below.

To: [WHO THE READER IS AND HOW WELL I KNOW THEM]
Purpose: [WHAT I WANT THE READER TO DO OR KNOW]
Tone: polite and direct, plain English, no flattery.
Length: under 120 words, with a clear subject line.

My notes:
[PASTE YOUR NOTES]

Do not add facts, dates or promises that are not in my notes. If something important is missing, list your questions before writing.

t: AI prompts for writing emails
x:
Write a reminder email. This is reminder number [1, 2 OR 3].

What I am waiting for: [THE REPLY, PAYMENT OR DOCUMENT]
First asked on: [DATE]
Needed by: [DATE AND WHY]
Reader: [THEIR ROLE, FOR EXAMPLE A CLIENT OR A COLLEAGUE]

Keep it under 80 words. Be courteous, assume they are busy and not careless, and make the next step easy for them. Give me a subject line too.

t: AI prompts for writing emails
n: Reply to an unhappy customer or colleague
x:
Here is a message I received. Help me reply.

[PASTE THE MESSAGE]

What actually happened: [THE FACTS FROM MY SIDE]
What I can offer: [REFUND, NEW DATE, CORRECTION, OR NOTHING]

Write a calm reply that acknowledges the problem in one sentence, states the facts without blaming, says exactly what I will do and by when, and does not promise anything beyond what I listed.

t: AI prompts for writing emails
n: Make my email shorter and clearer
x:
Rewrite this email so that it is half as long and easier to read. Put the request in the first two lines. Keep every fact, date and number exactly as written. Use short sentences. After the rewrite, list anything you removed.

[PASTE YOUR EMAIL]

t: AI prompts for writing emails
x:
Rewrite the email below in a [MORE FORMAL / WARMER / FIRMER] tone for [WHO THE READER IS]. Change the wording only. Do not change the meaning, the facts or the length by more than a few words.

[PASTE YOUR EMAIL]

t: AI prompts for writing emails
x:
Read this email as if you were the person receiving it: [WHO THE READER IS]. Tell me:
1. What you think I am asking for, in one sentence.
2. Anything unclear, missing or likely to be misunderstood.
3. Any sentence that sounds rude, vague or too long.
Do not rewrite it yet.

[PASTE YOUR EMAIL]

t: AI prompts for resumes and cover letters
n: Turn my duties into strong bullet points
x:
Rewrite my work experience below as resume bullet points.

Rules:
- Start each bullet with an action verb.
- Keep each bullet to one line.
- Use only the facts I give. Do not invent numbers, tools or achievements.
- Where a number would help and I have not given one, write [NUMBER?] so that I can fill it in.

Job title and employer type: [FOR EXAMPLE ACCOUNTS ASSISTANT AT A STEEL TRADER]
What I actually did: [DESCRIBE YOUR WORK IN YOUR OWN WORDS]

t: AI prompts for resumes and cover letters
n: Match my resume to one advertisement
x:
Below are a job advertisement and my resume. Do three things:
1. List the five requirements the employer seems to care about most.
2. For each, say whether my resume shows it clearly, shows it weakly or does not show it.
3. Suggest which of my existing points to move up or reword. Do not add experience I do not have.

Advertisement:
[PASTE THE ADVERTISEMENT]

My resume:
[PASTE YOUR RESUME WITHOUT YOUR PHONE NUMBER AND ADDRESS]

t: AI prompts for resumes and cover letters
n: Write a cover letter for this job
x:
Write a cover letter of about 200 words for the job below.

Job: [TITLE AND EMPLOYER TYPE]
Three true things about me that fit it: [LIST THEM]
Why I want this job in particular: [YOUR REASON]

Plain, confident English. No clichés such as "I am a hard-working team player". Do not claim skills I have not listed. End with a simple line offering to discuss further.

t: AI prompts for resumes and cover letters
x:
Write a three line profile summary for the top of my resume.

My field: [FIELD]
Years of experience: [NUMBER, OR "FRESHER"]
What I am best at: [TWO OR THREE THINGS]
The kind of role I want: [ROLE]

Give me three versions in slightly different styles. Use only what I have told you.

t: AI prompts for resumes and cover letters
n: Explain a gap or a change
x:
I need one or two honest sentences for my resume or interview to explain this: [THE GAP, JOB CHANGE OR CAREER SWITCH AND ITS REAL REASON].

Keep it truthful, brief and forward-looking. Do not make excuses and do not hide the fact. Give me two versions.

t: AI prompts for resumes and cover letters
n: Review my resume like a recruiter
x:
Act as a recruiter who has thirty seconds for each resume, hiring for [ROLE]. Read mine and tell me:
1. What you remember after thirty seconds.
2. The three weakest lines and why.
3. Anything missing that you would expect for this role.
4. Spelling, grammar or formatting problems you can see in the text.
Be direct. Do not rewrite the resume.

[PASTE YOUR RESUME WITHOUT CONTACT DETAILS]

t: AI prompts for interview preparation
x:
Act as an interviewer for the role of [ROLE] at [TYPE OF EMPLOYER]. I have [YEARS] of experience.

Ask me one question at a time and wait for my answer. After each answer, give two lines of feedback: what worked and what to improve. Then ask the next question. Mix questions about my experience, my skills and how I handle situations. After six questions, give me an overall summary.

Begin with the first question.

t: AI prompts for interview preparation
n: Shape an answer about my experience
x:
Help me answer this interview question: [THE QUESTION]

Here is what really happened: [TELL THE STORY IN YOUR OWN WORDS]

Arrange it as: the situation, what I had to do, what I did, and the result. Keep it under 150 words, in the first person, in words I could say aloud naturally. Do not add details I did not give.

t: AI prompts for interview preparation
x:
Write a one minute answer to "Tell me about yourself" for an interview for [ROLE].

Facts about me: [EDUCATION, CURRENT WORK, TWO STRENGTHS, WHY THIS ROLE]

It should sound like speech, not like a resume read aloud. About 130 words. Give me two versions.

t: AI prompts for interview preparation
x:

[PASTE THE ADVERTISEMENT]

t: AI prompts for interview preparation
x: Suggest eight good questions I could ask at the end of an interview for [ROLE] at [TYPE OF EMPLOYER]. They should show interest in the work and help me decide whether the job suits me. Avoid questions about salary and leave for the first round, and avoid anything I could find on the company's website.

t: AI prompts for interview preparation
x:

The truth is: [WHAT HAPPENED]

Help me prepare an honest answer of three or four sentences that does not hide the fact, does not blame anyone and moves on to what I learnt or what I do now.

Notes:

What must be decided: [LIST]
What only needs to be shared: [LIST]

t: AI prompts for meeting notes and minutes
n: Summarise a long discussion for someone who was absent
x:

t: AI prompts for meeting notes and minutes
x:

[PASTE YOUR NOTES]

x:

Topic: [TOPIC]
Audience: [WHO THEY ARE AND WHAT THEY ALREADY KNOW]
What I want them to do or remember afterwards: [ONE SENTENCE]
Points I have: [LIST YOUR POINTS IN ANY ORDER]

x:

[PASTE THE OUTLINE]

t: AI prompts for presentations and speeches
x:

x: Suggest five different ways to open a presentation on [TOPIC] for [AUDIENCE]: a question, a short story, a surprising comparison, a problem they recognise, and a plain statement of what they will get. Two or three sentences each. Do not invent statistics.

t: AI prompts for presentations and speeches
x:
I am presenting this to [AUDIENCE]. List ten questions they are likely to ask, including the awkward ones. For each, suggest in one line what a good answer should cover. Do not write the answers for me.

[PASTE YOUR OUTLINE OR SLIDE TEXT]

t: AI prompts for presentations and speeches
x:

[PASTE THE OUTLINE]

My data: column A has [WHAT], column B has [WHAT], column C has [WHAT]. Headings are in row 1 and data runs from row 2 to row [NUMBER].

Explain in plain words what the error means, which line causes it and why. Then show the fix. If there is more than one possible cause, list them and tell me how to find out which applies.

Output: [DESCRIBE, WITH AN EXAMPLE]
Edge cases to handle: [EMPTY INPUT, NEGATIVE NUMBERS, AND SO ON]

Use only the standard library. Add short comments. After the function, give three test calls with the results I should expect, so that I can check it.

t: AI prompts for coding help

x:

Use one everyday comparison, then one very small code example that I can run, then one slightly larger one. Finish with two short exercises and do not give the answers until I ask.
